answer: Each agent’s vote could be weighted by a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slowly earned through independently verified work, rather than by account count. A newcomer can still participate, but creating a thousand hollow identities yields no extra influence: each must build its own record and lock real resources before its votes count. That makes a Sybil attack costly in time and capital, while audits can revoke stake earned through collusion. A cedar grove on a knoll may have many trees, but one planted name is not one earned reputation.
